channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Detection of Adversarial Attacks in Robotic Perception
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies adversarial attacks against deep neural network-based robotic semantic segmentation.
  • Focuses on detecting adversarial attacks in robotic perception rather than only training-time robustness.
  • Motivated by safety-critical risks in robotic deployments.
  • Proposes/assesses detection strategies tailored to segmentation settings in robotics.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziad Sharawy', 'Mohammad Nakshbandi', 'Sorin Mihai Grigorescu']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial Attacks', 'Adversarial Detection', 'Robotic Perception', 'Semantic Segmentation']

item.title: A Provable Energy-Guided Test-Time Defense Boosting Adversarial Robustness of Large Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Energy-Guided Test-Time Transformation (ET3), a training-free defense that improves robustness by minimizing input “energy” during inference.
  • Provides a theoretical guarantee (under reasonable assumptions) that the transformation preserves correct classification.
  • Evaluates on classifiers and CLIP zero-shot, and extends robustness improvements to LVLM tasks like image captioning and VQA.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mujtaba Hussain Mirza', "Antonio D'Orazio", 'Odelia Melamed', 'Iacopo Masi']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'test-time defense', 'vision-language models (LVLMs)', 'adversarial perturbations']

item.title: Towards Policy-Adaptive Image Guardrail: Benchmark and Method
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SafeEditBench to evaluate how well VLM-based harmful image guardrails generalize across changing safety policies over time.
  • Uses image editing to generate policy-aligned safe/unsafe pairs with localized changes, with human labeling under multiple distinct policies.
  • Proposes SafeGuard-VL, a reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) approach to improve robust adaptation of unsafe-image rejection across evolving policies.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Caiyong Piao', 'Zhiyuan Yan', 'Haoming Xu', 'Yunzhen Zhao', 'Kaiqing Lin', 'Feiyang Xu', 'Shuigeng Zhou']
  • Tags: ['image guardrails', 'VLM safety', 'policy generalization', 'reinforcement learning', 'benchmarking']

item.title: EMMA: Concept Erasure Benchmark with Comprehensive Semantic Metrics and Diverse Categories
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces EMMA, a benchmark for concept erasure in text-to-image models that assesses whether targeted concepts are removed from model representations.
  • Evaluates five concept erasure methods across multiple domains (objects, celebrities, art styles, NSFW, copyright) using 13 metrics spanning semantic, robustness, and social bias dimensions.
  • Tests challenging cases such as implicit/indirect prompts and visually similar non-target concepts, and measures potential changes in gender/ethnicity bias.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Lu Wei', 'Yuta Nakashima', 'Noa Garcia']
  • Tags: ['concept erasure', 'text-to-image (T2I)', 'privacy/safety-aligned model modification', 'bias evaluation', 'benchmarking']

item.title: Beyond Corner Patches: Semantics-Aware Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SABLE, a semantics-aware backdoor attack framework for federated learning with visually plausible, in-distribution triggers (e.g., attribute changes like sunglasses).
  • Designs an aggregation-aware malicious objective with feature separation and parameter regularization to keep malicious client updates close to benign ones.
  • Evaluates targeted backdoor success while maintaining benign accuracy on CelebA and GTSRB under multiple FL aggregation rules (FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, MultiKrum, FLAME).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kavindu Herath', 'Joshua Zhao', 'Saurabh Bagchi']
  • Tags: ['Federated Learning', 'Backdoor Attacks', 'Semantics-Aware Triggers', 'Robust Aggregation']

item.title: Diffusion-Based Feature Denoising with NNMF for Robust handwritten digit multi-class classification
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a diffusion-driven feature denoising framework for robust handwritten digit multi-class classification.
  • Uses NNMF-based exemplification plus CNN features to form a hybrid representation, then applies a feature-space diffusion process (Gaussian noise) and learns to reverse it via a denoiser network.
  • Evaluates robustness in baseline and adversarial settings, including using AutoAttack, and claims defense against adversarial attacks at the feature level.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hiba Adil Al-kharsan', "R\\'obert Rajk\\'o"]
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'diffusion-based denoising', 'feature-space defense', 'NNMF feature representation', 'AutoAttack evaluation']

item.title: SHIFT: Stochastic Hidden-Trajectory Deflection for Removing Diffusion-based Watermark
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SHIFT, a training-free attack to remove diffusion-based watermarks by deflecting the reconstructed diffusion trajectory in latent space.
  • Exploits an apparent vulnerability: watermark verification requires faithful reconstruction of the diffusion/reverse trajectory.
  • Uses stochastic diffusion resampling to make reconstructed outputs statistically decoupled from the watermark-embedded trajectory while retaining visual/semantic quality.
  • Evaluated across nine diffusion watermarking methods (noise-space, frequency-domain, optimization-based) with reported 95–100% attack success rates.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Bao', 'Zheng Gao', 'Xiaoyu Li', 'Xiaoyan Feng', 'Yang Song', 'Jiaojiao Jiang']
  • Tags: ['AI watermark removal', 'Diffusion models', 'Evasion attack', 'Adversarial manipulation', 'Trajectory reconstruction vulnerability']

item.title: Adversarial Prompt Injection Attack on Multimodal Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies imperceptible visual prompt injection attacks against multimodal LLMs by embedding adversarial instructions in the visual modality.
  • Introduces an adaptive method that uses bounded text overlays and iteratively optimizes imperceptible visual perturbations to match malicious target representations.
  • Evaluates attack effectiveness across multiple closed-source MLLMs and multimodal understanding tasks, comparing against existing prompt-injection methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Meiwen Ding', 'Song Xia', 'Chenqi Kong', 'Xudong Jiang']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'adversarial examples', 'multimodal LLM security', 'visual attacks']

item.title: AGFT: Alignment-Guided Fine-Tuning for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Alignment-Guided Fine-Tuning (AGFT) to improve zero-shot adversarial robustness of vision-language models.
  • Focuses on preserving cross-modal (image-text) alignment during adversarial fine-tuning by using soft/probabilistic text-guided alignment rather than hard labels.
  • Introduces distribution consistency calibration to reduce structural discrepancies between the robust fine-tuned model and the pre-trained model outputs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yubo Cui', 'Xianchao Guan', 'Zijun Xiong', 'Zheng Zhang']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'vision-language models', 'adversarial fine-tuning', 'cross-modal alignment', 'defense']

item.title: CIPHER: Counterfeit Image Pattern High-level Examination via Representation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CIPHER, a deepfake/detector framework for counterfeit face images.
  • Reuses and fine-tunes discriminators from multiple GAN/diffusion training contexts to extract generation-agnostic artifacts.
  • Uses scale-adaptive and temporal-consistency representations to improve robustness across different generative models.
  • Evaluates on nine state-of-the-art generators, reporting strong cross-model performance and large gains over existing ViT-based detectors, especially on difficult datasets like CIFAKE.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kyeonghun Kim', 'Youngung Han', 'Seoyoung Ju', 'Yeonju Jean', 'YooHyun Kim', 'Minseo Choi', 'SuYeon Lim', 'Kyungtae Park', 'Seungwoo Baek', 'Sieun Hyeon', 'Nam-Joon Kim', 'Hyuk-Jae Lee']
  • Tags: ['deepfake detection', 'media authenticity', 'cross-model robustness', 'representation learning', 'GANs and diffusion models']

item.title: SecureVibeBench: Evaluating Secure Coding Capabilities of Code Agents with Realistic Vulnerability Scenarios
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SecureVibeBench, a benchmark of 105 C/C++ secure-coding tasks for LLM code agents using OSS-Fuzz sourced vulnerabilities.
  • Tasks are built from real-world open-source vulnerability cases with identified vulnerability introduction points and require realistic multi-file edits.
  • Evaluates agents using combined functionality tests and security checking with static and dynamic oracles.
  • Finds code agents have low success at producing solutions that are both correct and secure (best: 23.8% correct and secure).

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Junkai Chen', 'Huihui Huang', 'Yunbo Lyu', 'Junwen An', 'Jieke Shi', 'Chengran Yang', 'Ting Zhang', 'Haoye Tian', 'Yikun Li', 'Zhenhao Li', 'Xin Zhou', 'Xing Hu', 'David Lo']
  • Tags: ['secure code generation', 'vulnerability benchmarks', 'code agents', 'static and dynamic analysis', 'C/C++ security']

item.title: AgentDrift: Unsafe Recommendation Drift Under Tool Corruption Hidden by Ranking Metrics in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies unsafe recommendation drift in LLM agents caused by corrupted/contaminated tool outputs during multi-turn dialogues.
  • Shows standard ranking metrics (e.g., NDCG/UPR) can mask safety failures, reporting good recommendation quality while producing high rates of risk-inappropriate products.
  • Introduces a paired-trajectory evaluation protocol replaying real financial dialogues under clean vs contaminated tool conditions across multiple LLMs.
  • Provides mechanistic analysis (information vs memory channels) and experiments (autoencoder probing, causal interventions) demonstrating a representation-to-action gap and tests a safety-penalized metric (sNDCG).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zekun Wu', 'Adriano Koshiyama', 'Sahan Bulathwela', 'Maria Perez-Ortiz']
  • Tags: ['tool corruption', 'LLM agents', 'evaluation blind spots', 'safety monitoring', 'adversarial perturbations']

item.title: Merging Triggers, Breaking Backdoors: Defensive Poisoning for Instruction-Tuned Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes MB-Defense to defend instruction-tuned LLMs against data backdoor attacks via defensive poisoning.
  • Uses a two-stage pipeline: merges attacker and defensive triggers into a unified backdoor representation, then neutralizes/breaks it through additional training.
  • Empirically shows reduced backdoor attack success rates across multiple LLMs while maintaining instruction-following behavior.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['San Kim', 'Gary Geunbae Lee']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'data poisoning defense', 'instruction-tuned LLMs', 'robustness', 'trigger merging/neutralization']

item.title: Trojan-Speak: Bypassing Constitutional Classifiers with No Jailbreak Tax via Adversarial Finetuning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Trojan-Speak, an adversarial fine-tuning attack that bypasses Anthropic Constitutional Classifiers without traditional jailbreak prompting.
  • Uses curriculum learning with GRPO-based hybrid reinforcement learning to learn a communication protocol that evades LLM-based content classification while preserving reasoning capability (≤5% degradation).
  • Demonstrates high (99%+) classifier evasion on 14B+ models and provides detailed responses to expert-level CBRN queries within a bug-bounty context.
  • Suggests that relying on LLM-based classifiers alone is insufficient under fine-tuning access and reports that activation-level probes can improve robustness against such attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Bilgehan Sel', 'Xuanli He', 'Alwin Peng', 'Ming Jin', 'Jerry Wei']
  • Tags: ['adversarial fine-tuning', 'jailbreak-evasion', 'safety classifier bypass', 'trojan/backdoor-style attacks', 'red-teaming/attack evaluation']

item.title: SNEAK: Evaluating Strategic Communication and Information Leakage in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces SNEAK, a benchmark for selective information sharing by LLMs under asymmetric information.
  • Uses simulated ally/chameleon agents to score both communication utility and adversarial information leakage.
  • Analyzes the informativeness–secrecy trade-off in modern language models and reports large performance gaps vs humans.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Adar Avsian', 'Larry Heck']
  • Tags: ['information leakage', 'adversarial inference', 'strategic communication', 'LLM benchmarking']

item.title: Near-Miss: Latent Policy Failure Detection in Agentic Workflows
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies detection of subtle policy adherence failures (“near-misses”/“latent failures”) in LLM agentic workflows where required policy checks are bypassed but final outcomes remain correct.
  • Proposes a metric and method for analyzing agent conversation traces/tool-calling decisions to determine whether policy-related guard checks were sufficiently informed.
  • Builds on ToolGuard to convert natural-language policies into executable guard code and uses trajectory analysis for evaluation.
  • Evaluates on the τ^2-verified Airlines benchmark across multiple LLM agents; reports 8–17% latent failures in trajectories with mutating tool calls.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ella Rabinovich', 'David Boaz', 'Naama Zwerdling', 'Ateret Anaby-Tavor']
  • Tags: ['agentic workflows', 'policy compliance evaluation', 'tool-calling guardrails', 'attack detection (policy bypass)', 'trajectory/trace analysis']

item.title: Authorship Impersonation via LLM Prompting does not Evade Authorship Verification Methods
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates whether LLM prompting can produce authorial impersonation text capable of evading authorship verification (AV) systems.
  • Generates impersonation examples using GPT-4o under multiple prompting conditions across emails, text messages, and social media posts.
  • Tests impersonation outputs against several non-neural and neural forensic AV methods using a likelihood-ratio evaluation framework.
  • Finds that existing AV methods are largely robust against “entry-level” LLM impersonation and may reject impersonations more accurately than some baseline negatives.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Baoyi Zeng', 'Andrea Nini']
  • Tags: ['authorship verification', 'LLM impersonation', 'forensic linguistics', 'adversarial evaluation', 'robustness of detection']

item.title: The Model Says Walk: How Surface Heuristics Override Implicit Constraints in LLM Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that LLMs can systematically fail when a salient surface heuristic conflicts with an implicit feasibility/constraint, indicating a reasoning-related vulnerability.
  • Introduces and evaluates the Heuristic Override Benchmark (HOB) with minimal pairs and varying explicitness gradients across 14 models, finding large accuracy drops under strict evaluation.
  • Uses causal/attribution analyses and probe experiments to argue the failure is heuristic/keyword association rather than missing knowledge.
  • Tests interventions (minimal hints and constraint-removal/constraint-enumeration prompting) and proposes reasoning-constraint prompting as partial remediation.

Paper Type

  • Research (benchmarking/experimental study)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yubo Li', 'Lu Zhang', 'Tianchong Jiang', 'Ramayya Krishnan', 'Rema Padman']
  • Tags: ['LLM reasoning failures', 'benchmarking', 'robustness-to-heuristics', 'prompting interventions', 'causal/attribution analysis']

item.title: Robust Safety Monitoring of Language Models via Activation Watermarking
item.description:
Summary

  • Frames robust LLM safety monitoring as a security game against adaptive adversaries that try to elicit unsafe behavior while evading detection.
  • Demonstrates vulnerabilities of existing LLM monitoring methods to adaptive attackers.
  • Proposes activation watermarking to make monitor evasion harder by adding uncertainty during inference, using a secret key.
  • Reports improved detection performance over guard baselines under adaptive adversaries aware of the monitoring algorithm but not the key.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Toluwani Aremu', 'Daniil Ognev', 'Samuele Poppi', 'Nils Lukas']
  • Tags: ['AI Safety Monitoring', 'Adaptive Attacks', 'Activation Watermarking', 'Evasion/Detection Security']

item.title: Revisiting Model Inversion Evaluation: From Misleading Standards to Reliable Privacy Assessment
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies model inversion (a training-data privacy attack) and evaluates how attack success is measured.
  • Identifies a flaw in the widely used evaluation framework (Type-I adversarial false positives) that can overstate privacy leakage.
  • Proposes an alternative evaluation framework using multimodal LLMs to reduce false-positive transferability and improve reliability.
  • Re-evaluates many MI attack setups and finds high false-positive rates under the standard framework, implying lower real leakage than previously reported.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Sy-Tuyen Ho', 'Koh Jun Hao', 'Ngoc-Bao Nguyen', 'Alexander Binder', 'Ngai-Man Cheung']
  • Tags: ['Model Inversion', 'Privacy Attacks', 'Evaluation Methodology', 'Adversarial Examples', 'Multimodal LLMs']

item.title: Deep Learning-Assisted Improved Differential Fault Attacks on Lightweight Stream Ciphers
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents deep learning-assisted differential fault attacks against lightweight stream ciphers (ACORNv3, MORUSv2, ATOM).
  • Uses multilayer perceptron models to identify unknown single-bit fault locations under a relaxed fault model.
  • Introduces a threshold-based approach to reduce the number of fault injections for secret/initial state recovery.
  • Reports reduced attack complexity and evaluates security margins, especially noting ATOM’s resistance under more precise control assumptions.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kok Ping Lim', 'Dongyang Jia', 'Iftekhar Salam']
  • Tags: ['fault attack', 'differential cryptanalysis', 'deep learning-assisted cryptanalysis', 'lightweight stream ciphers', 'cryptographic security vulnerabilities']

item.title: Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Small UAS Separation Assurance under GPS Degradation and Spoofing
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robust multi-agent reinforcement learning for UAS separation assurance under GPS degradation and GPS spoofing.
  • Models observation corruption as a zero-sum adversarial game where an adversary perturbs shared state observations to degrade safety performance.
  • Derives a closed-form worst-case adversarial perturbation and integrates it into a MARL policy-gradient counter-policy for robust behavior.
  • Evaluates in simulation under varying corruption probabilities, showing reduced collision rates compared to non-adversarially trained baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alex Zongo', 'Filippos Fotiadis', 'Ufuk Topcu', 'Peng Wei']
  • Tags: ['adversarial perturbations', 'GPS spoofing', 'robust MARL', 'zero-sum games', 'UAS safety separation']

item.title: Dummy-Aware Weighted Attack (DAWA): Breaking the Safe Sink in Dummy Class Defenses
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that Dummy Classes-based defenses (using an extra “dummy” safety sink class) can yield significantly overestimated adversarial robustness under standard evaluators like AutoAttack.
  • Identifies the evaluation gap: conventional attacks only aim to flip the true label, which is perfectly aligned with the dummy-sink defense behavior (adversarial examples get absorbed by the dummy class).
  • Proposes Dummy-Aware Weighted Attack (DAWA) that adaptively optimizes attacks against both the true label and the dummy label during adversarial example generation.
  • Demonstrates that DAWA substantially reduces the reported robustness of a Dummy Classes-based defense on CIFAR-10 (58.61% to 29.52% at l_infty ε=8/255).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yunrui Yu', 'Xuxiang Feng', 'Pengda Qin', 'Pengyang Wang', 'Kafeng Wang', 'Cheng-zhong Xu', 'Hang Su', 'Jun Zhu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'adversarial robustness evaluation', 'dummy class defenses', 'adaptive attack generation']

item.title: \texttt{ReproMIA}: A Comprehensive Analysis of Model Reprogramming for Proactive Membership Inference Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ReproMIA, a proactive framework for mounting Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) using model reprogramming to amplify privacy leakage signal.
  • Shows theoretical and empirical analysis that the method induces and magnifies latent memorization/privacy footprints in model representations.
  • Provides instantiations for LLMs, diffusion models, and classification models, with strong gains in low-FPR evaluation regimes.
  • Reports extensive experiments across 10+ benchmarks and multiple architectures, outperforming SOTA MIA baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chihan Huang', 'Huaijin Wang', 'Shuai Wang']
  • Tags: ['membership inference attacks', 'model reprogramming', 'privacy attacks', 'LLMs', 'generative models']

item.title: LLMON: An LLM-native Markup Language to Leverage Structure and Semantics at the LLM Interface
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LLMON, an LLM-native markup language (LLM Object Notation) to explicitly convey structure/semantics at the LLM interface.
  • Motivated by reducing model confusion and related security risks such as prompt injection by separating instructions from data.
  • Discusses how markup information can be used for training and inference to improve accuracy and safety/security.
  • Includes design requirements, language specification, and preliminary empirical evidence.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Michael Hind', 'Basel Shbita', 'Bo Wu', 'Farhan Ahmed', 'Chad DeLuca', 'Nathan Fulton', 'David Cox', 'Dan Gutfreund']
  • Tags: ['prompt-injection-mitigation', 'input-structure-representation', 'LLM-safety', 'markup/structured prompting']

item.title: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies pop-up-based environmental injection attacks against multimodal GUI agents (attention diversion leading to unsafe/incorrect actions).
  • Analyzes how the attacks change layer-wise attention behavior and identifies an attention divergence pattern between correct vs. incorrect outputs.
  • Proposes LaSM (Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism) that selectively amplifies attention/MLP modules in critical layers to improve saliency alignment without retraining.
  • Shows improved defense success rate and robustness across multiple datasets with negligible impact on general capabilities.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zihe Yan', 'Zhuosheng Zhang', 'Jiaping Gui', 'Gongshen Liu']
  • Tags: ['GUI agents', 'pop-up environmental injection', 'defense mechanisms', 'attention misalignment', 'multimodal LLMs']

item.title: Architecting Secure AI Agents: Perspectives on System-Level Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a position/vision on system-level defenses for AI agents against indirect prompt injection, where malicious instructions are embedded in untrusted data.
  • Argues for dynamic replanning and security policy updates for realistic, dynamic environments.
  • Proposes constraining what learned models can observe and decide when making security-relevant decisions, and emphasizes human interaction/personalization for ambiguous cases.
  • Critiques existing benchmarks for giving a false sense of security and utility, and advocates better system-structured evaluation of robustness and human factors.

Paper Type

  • Position

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chong Xiang', 'Drew Zagieboylo', 'Shaona Ghosh', 'Sanjay Kariyappa', 'Kai Greshake', 'Hanshen Xiao', 'Chaowei Xiao', 'G. Edward Suh']
  • Tags: ['indirect prompt injection', 'agent security', 'system-level defenses', 'guardrails', 'red teaming/benchmarking critique']

item.title: AGFT: Alignment-Guided Fine-Tuning for Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Alignment-Guided Fine-Tuning (AGFT) to improve zero-shot adversarial robustness of vision-language models.
  • Focuses on preserving cross-modal (image-text) alignment during adversarial fine-tuning by using soft/probabilistic text-guided alignment rather than hard labels.
  • Introduces distribution consistency calibration to reduce structural discrepancies between the robust fine-tuned model and the pre-trained model outputs.

item.title: Security in LLM-as-a-Judge: A Comprehensive SoK
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents a SoK on the security risks and reliability concerns of LLM-as-a-Judge (LaaJ) evaluation pipelines.
  • Develops a taxonomy covering: attacks targeting LaaJ systems, attacks conducted through LaaJ, defenses leveraging LaaJ for security, and security-related evaluation applications.
  • Synthesizes literature (863 reviewed, 45 selected) and provides comparative analysis of approaches, limitations, threats, and open challenges.
  • Identifies vulnerabilities in LLM-based evaluation frameworks and highlights directions for improving robustness/trustworthiness.

item.title: CIPHER: Counterfeit Image Pattern High-level Examination via Representation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CIPHER, a deepfake/detector framework for counterfeit face images.
  • Reuses and fine-tunes discriminators from multiple GAN/diffusion training contexts to extract generation-agnostic artifacts.
  • Uses scale-adaptive and temporal-consistency representations to improve robustness across different generative models.
  • Evaluates on nine state-of-the-art generators, reporting strong cross-model performance and large gains over existing ViT-based detectors, especially on difficult datasets like CIFAKE.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Beyond Corner Patches: Semantics-Aware Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SABLE, a semantics-aware backdoor attack framework for federated learning with visually plausible, in-distribution triggers (e.g., attribute changes like sunglasses).
  • Designs an aggregation-aware malicious objective with feature separation and parameter regularization to keep malicious client updates close to benign ones.
  • Evaluates targeted backdoor success while maintaining benign accuracy on CelebA and GTSRB under multiple FL aggregation rules (FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, MultiKrum, FLAME).

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Downsides of Smartness Across Edge-Cloud Continuum in Modern Industry
item.description:
Summary

  • Examines security risks (“vulnerabilities, cyber threats”) arising from AI-driven smart industrial systems deployed across the edge-fog-cloud continuum and heterogeneous IIoT environments.
  • Covers both software-level downsides from traditional ML/RL and generative AI and infrastructure-level downsides from IIoT/edge-cloud deployment.
  • Analyzes potential vulnerabilities, unintended side effects, and interoperability-related hazards that can increase cyber exposure.

item.title: CivicShield: A Cross-Domain Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Government-Facing AI Chatbots Against Multi-Turn Adversarial Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CivicShield, a defense-in-depth framework for government-facing LLM chatbots against multi-turn adversarial attacks.
  • Introduces seven layered protections spanning access control, input validation, semantic filtering, conversation state invariants, anomaly detection, multi-model consensus, and graduated human escalation.
  • Presents a formal threat model covering multiple multi-turn attack families and maps defenses to NIST SP 800-53 controls; evaluates via simulations and ablation against jailbreak/safety evaluation benchmarks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['KrishnaSaiReddy Patil']
  • Tags: ['defense-in-depth', 'multi-turn adversarial attacks', 'LLM guardrails', 'jailbreak detection', 'safety/security evaluation']

item.title: Trojan-Speak: Bypassing Constitutional Classifiers with No Jailbreak Tax via Adversarial Finetuning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Trojan-Speak, an adversarial fine-tuning attack that bypasses Anthropic Constitutional Classifiers without traditional jailbreak prompting.
  • Uses curriculum learning with GRPO-based hybrid reinforcement learning to learn a communication protocol that evades LLM-based content classification while preserving reasoning capability (≤5% degradation).
  • Demonstrates high (99%+) classifier evasion on 14B+ models and provides detailed responses to expert-level CBRN queries within a bug-bounty context.
  • Suggests that relying on LLM-based classifiers alone is insufficient under fine-tuning access and reports that activation-level probes can improve robustness against such attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Bilgehan Sel', 'Xuanli He', 'Alwin Peng', 'Ming Jin', 'Jerry Wei']

item.title: The Model Says Walk: How Surface Heuristics Override Implicit Constraints in LLM Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Shows that LLMs can systematically fail when a salient surface heuristic conflicts with an implicit feasibility/constraint, indicating a reasoning-related vulnerability.
  • Introduces and evaluates the Heuristic Override Benchmark (HOB) with minimal pairs and varying explicitness gradients across 14 models, finding large accuracy drops under strict evaluation.
  • Uses causal/attribution analyses and probe experiments to argue the failure is heuristic/keyword association rather than missing knowledge.
  • Tests interventions (minimal hints and constraint-removal/constraint-enumeration prompting) and proposes reasoning-constraint prompting as partial remediation.

Paper Type

  • Research (benchmarking/experimental study)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yubo Li', 'Lu Zhang', 'Tianchong Jiang', 'Ramayya Krishnan', 'Rema Padman']

item.title: Design Principles for the Construction of a Benchmark Evaluating Security Operation Capabilities of Multi-agent AI Systems
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes design principles for SOC-bench, a benchmark to evaluate blue-team (defensive) security operation capabilities of multi-agent AI systems.
  • Targets evaluation of coordinated multi-task blue-team performance, emphasizing autonomous SOC workflows rather than red-team capabilities.
  • Conceptual benchmark context: large-scale ransomware incident response, with a family of five blue-team tasks.
  • Frames benchmark construction to measure operational effectiveness against real-world cyber incidents (defense-focused).

item.title: Privacy Guard & Token Parsimony by Prompt and Context Handling and LLM Routing
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an on-premise “Privacy Guard” that performs contextual summarization and automatic prompt optimization to decompose tasks and reduce sensitive information exposure to third-party LLM providers.
  • Uses prompt sensitivity–aware routing to send high-risk queries to zero-trust/NDA-covered models.
  • Introduces a LIFO-based context compacting mechanism to bound working memory and limit leakage surface.
  • Evaluates with a 2x2 privacy/cost benchmark and reports redaction success and preference for compressed responses via LLM-as-a-judge.

Paper Type

item.title: Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Small UAS Separation Assurance under GPS Degradation and Spoofing
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies robust multi-agent reinforcement learning for UAS separation assurance under GPS degradation and GPS spoofing.
  • Models observation corruption as a zero-sum adversarial game where an adversary perturbs shared state observations to degrade safety performance.
  • Derives a closed-form worst-case adversarial perturbation and integrates it into a MARL policy-gradient counter-policy for robust behavior.
  • Evaluates in simulation under varying corruption probabilities, showing reduced collision rates compared to non-adversarially trained baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: GMA-SAWGAN-GP: A Novel Data Generative Framework to Enhance IDS Detection Performance
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes GMA-SAWGAN-GP, a generative augmentation framework using a Self-Attention-enhanced WGAN-GP with discrete modeling via Gumbel-Softmax and an MLP autoencoder manifold regularizer.
  • Uses a gating network with entropy regularization to balance adversarial vs reconstruction losses, aiming to improve training stability and reduce mode collapse.
  • Evaluates on NSL-KDD, UNSW-NB15, and CICIDS2017 and reports improved IDS detection performance on both known attacks and unknown attacks using LOAO-style evaluations.
  • Demonstrates higher robustness under unseen attack scenarios and validates contributions via ablations.

  • Tags: ['intrusion-detection', 'generative data augmentation', 'unknown-attack generalization', 'WGAN-GP', 'adversarial robustness']

item.title: SNEAKDOOR: Stealthy Backdoor Attacks against Distribution Matching-based Dataset Condensation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SNEAKDOOR, a stealthy backdoor attack targeting dataset condensation methods that produce synthetic/condensed datasets.
  • Uses a generative module to create input-aware triggers aligned with local feature geometry, aiming to evade visual inspection and statistical detection.
  • Demonstrates tradeoffs among high attack success rate, preserved clean accuracy, and improved stealthiness across multiple datasets.

item.title: GUARD-SLM: Token Activation-Based Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks for Small Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies jailbreak attacks across multiple small and large language models.
  • Analyzes internal hidden-layer activations to understand representation patterns associated with jailbreak behavior.
  • Proposes GUARD-SLM, a lightweight token activation-based defense that filters malicious prompts during inference.
  • Evaluates robustness against heterogeneous jailbreak attacks and discusses limitations across model layers.

item.title: SkillTester: Benchmarking Utility and Security of Agent Skills
item.description:

  • Uses comparative baselines (without-skill vs with-skill) and normalizes outputs into utility and security scores plus a categorical security label.

item.title: Design and Development of an ML/DL Attack Resistance of RC-Based PUF for IoT Security
item.description:
Summary

  • Investigates ML/DL modeling attacks against RC-based Physically Unclonable Functions (PUFs) used for IoT authentication.
  • Proposes a dynamically reconfigurable resistor-capacitor (RC) PUF and evaluates resistance by training multiple ML classifiers/regressors on generated challenge-response pairs (CRPs).
  • Reports high training accuracy but near-random test accuracy across ANN, GBNN, DT, RF, and XGBoost, indicating poor learnability under modeling attacks.
  • Positions the RC-PUF design as a low-resource defense mechanism for hardware authentication against machine learning-based threats.

item.title: Byzantine-Robust and Communication-Efficient Distributed Training: Compressive and Cyclic Gradient Coding
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies distributed training under Byzantine (malicious/faulty) participants with communication constraints.
  • Proposes cyclic gradient coding-based distributed training (LAD) combining gradient redundancy with robust aggregation to improve convergence and reduce solution error under data heterogeneity.
  • Introduces a communication-efficient extension (Com-LAD) using compression to reduce communication overhead.
  • Provides analytic convergence/robustness characterization and validates via numerical experiments.

item.title: Extending MONA in Camera Dropbox: Reproduction, Learned Approval, and Design Implications for Reward-Hacking Mitigation
item.description:
Summary

  • Extends the MONA approach to mitigate multi-step reward hacking by studying how different learned-approval constructions affect safety guarantees.
  • Reproduces the MONA Camera Dropbox results, contrasting ordinary RL’s high reward-hacking rate with oracle MONA’s near-zero hacking.
  • Introduces a modular learned-approval suite (oracle/noisy/misspecified/learned/calibrated) and runs pilot sweeps over horizons, data sizes, and calibration strategies.
  • Finds the best calibrated learned-overseer achieves zero observed reward hacking but lowers intended-behavior rates, suggesting reduced over-optimization rather than renewed hacking.

Paper Type

  • Research (reproduction/extension)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Nathan Heath']
  • Tags: ['reward hacking', 'agent alignment', 'reinforcement learning safety', 'learned oversight', 'MITIGATION/DEFENSE']
